plain.li: Dreamt my Pokémon started to glow, brighter and brighter, and when the light faded it was something I'd never seen, and it still knew me.
My Pokémon evolved three times in one night, and each time it turned around to check I was still watching.
[child] I dreamt my Pokémon got so big it could carry me to the moon. We went. It was nice.

warm.li: In my dream my Pokémon evolved, and the first thing it did was come and lean against me, the way it always does.

cheerful.li: My Pokémon evolved in my dream and learned a move that made flowers grow everywhere!

cold.li: A dream about evolution. I have three new ideas for its training.

ColonyCouncil.DreamDef.label: a dream of a legendary Pokémon

plain.li: Dreamt a great bird of ice flew over the colony so low its wings frosted the roofs, and it looked straight at me.
In the dream something huge moved under the earth, and every Pokémon in the colony turned to face the same way.
The old legends, in my dream: a Pokémon made of lightning, standing on the ridge in a storm, waiting for someone worthy.

blunt.li: Dreamt of a legendary. Big. Watching. Gone at dawn.

gloomy.li: Something ancient was looking for me in the dream. I don't know if I want it to find me.

cold.li: A dream about a legendary Pokémon. The stories say they reward a full Pokédex. I'll look into it.

ColonyCouncil.DreamDef.label: a dream of an empty ball

plain.li: Dreamt I threw my ball to let my Pokémon out, and it opened empty, and kept opening empty however many times I threw it.
In the dream my Pokémon wouldn't come when I called. It just watched me from across the field like a stranger.
[afterraid] My Pokémon fainted in the fight and I couldn't reach it through the smoke.

warm.li: Dreamt I lost my Pokémon. I went and sat with it after I woke, until my hands stopped shaking.

blunt.li: Bad dream. Empty ball. Checked. It's fine.

gloomy.li: My Pokémon had forgotten me in the dream. I'm afraid that one day it will.

cold.li: An anxious dream about my Pokémon. I'll spend more time with it today.
